wave: ADL COMPILER -- close silent constraint/invariant evaluation gaps
wave_title: core/src/language/adl/mod.rs's parse_constraint_check silently returned an empty check list (no diagnostic) for any constraint/invariant body it did not recognize, and evaluate_constraints only ever iterated declared.constraints, never declared.invariants -- so an unrecognized constraint silently reported passed:true, and every invariant declaration was parsed, recorded, and then completely skipped by evaluation, never appearing in constraint_results at all.

generation_model.G_n: 06549c5a62 (test(census): verify source/role/activation against real donor data) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Adversarial code-reading of core/src/language/adl/mod.rs (the ADL compiler), an area not previously audited this session, after the dependency-census capability's known gaps (role/activation collapse, multi-line workspace.members, real-scale verification) were closed. Traced parse_constraint_check's two recognized patterns (`require materialized X`, and the `forall`/`where`/`require`/`==` shape) and found the fallback path returns Vec::new() with no AdlDiagnostic, unlike the established sibling function parse_relation, which returns Result<RelationDecl, AdlDiagnostic> with code ATLAS-E030 for the analogous unrecognized-syntax case. Following the empty Vec downstream into evaluate_constraints found `passed: diagnostics.is_empty()`, which is trivially true when checks is empty -- a constraint whose syntax was never understood reports as having passed. Grepping every reference to `invariants` in the same file then found a second, independent, and more severe defect: DeclaredGraph.invariants is populated during parsing but evaluate_constraints's `.map()` chain only iterates `declared.constraints` -- `declared.invariants` is read nowhere in the whole file except to populate it. Confirmed the real-world consequence via runtime/src/census/mod.rs (invariants are recorded as `Declared` SemanticFact but never as `ConstraintResult` facts) and apps/cli/src/main.rs (the `check` subcommand's ADL_CHECK_NOT_READY gate reads only report.diagnostics and report.constraint_results.passed, neither of which a violated invariant could ever populate).

priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity (priority 1) -- `.atlas/contracts/ARCHITECTURAL-INTEGRITY.md:155` states explicitly: 'If Atlas cannot evaluate a required hard invariant, the result is UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE, not PASS.' Both defects directly violated this canonical rule: an unrecognized constraint reported PASS instead of UNKNOWN, and every invariant was silently excluded from evaluation entirely rather than reported as unevaluated.

design_decisions.question: For unrecognized constraint/invariant syntax: drop the declaration entirely (matching parse_relation's behavior for unrecognized relations), or keep it with zero checks?
design_decisions.decision: Keep the declaration (as ConstraintDecl with empty checks), but diagnose it (ATLAS-E052) and never let it report passed:true. Unlike a relation, a constraint/invariant has a name with real provenance value -- recording that a constraint named X was declared but could not be understood is itself useful census evidence (an OBSERVED_BUT_NOT_UNDERSTOOD state in the standing loop's own epistemic vocabulary), whereas dropping it silently would erase that a declaration existed at all.

design_decisions.question: Diagnose only at parse time (ATLAS-E052), or also defensively at evaluation time?
design_decisions.decision: Both. parse_adl_source pushes ATLAS-E052 into the program's top-level diagnostics when parse_constraint_check returns Err (unrecognized or empty body). evaluate_constraints additionally never reports passed:true for a zero-check declaration -- it pushes a second diagnostic (ATLAS-E053) directly onto that declaration's own ConstraintResult and reports passed:false. This is defense-in-depth: the per-result diagnostic makes the specific broken constraint/invariant identifiable directly from constraint_results (which is what a human or tool scanning for 'what failed' would read), not only inferable from a separate top-level diagnostics list that doesn't name which constraint it came from as clearly in that data shape.

design_decisions.question: How to fix invariants never being evaluated: duplicate evaluate_constraints's logic for invariants, or merge?
design_decisions.decision: Merge -- `declared.constraints.iter().chain(declared.invariants.iter())`. Constraints and invariants already share one type (ConstraintDecl/ConstraintCheck) and were always intended to share evaluation semantics (both check declared-graph attribute/materialization conditions); the difference between them is declarative categorization (which is preserved separately via DeclaredGraph.constraints vs .invariants and the Constraint/Invariant AdlDeclaration variants), not evaluation logic. A duplicated second evaluation loop would be exactly the kind of duplicate semantic concept this session's own engineering-quality rules (avoid duplicate semantic concepts) warn against.

design_decisions.question: Should an empty constraint/invariant body ever be treated as a legitimate no-op (vacuously true)?
design_decisions.decision: No. The ADL grammar has no construct expressing an intentional no-op constraint, and treating empty-as-vacuously-true is exactly the silent-pass failure mode being fixed. Any zero-check declaration is treated uniformly as evaluation-impossible, matching the ARCHITECTURAL-INTEGRITY.md rule cited above.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Every constraint AND every invariant declared in ADL source is evaluated by the same pass and appears in constraint_results; a declaration whose syntax was not recognized is diagnosed (ATLAS-E052) and never reports passed:true (ATLAS-E053 as defense-in-depth); a genuinely satisfied or violated constraint/invariant behaves identically to before this change (no regression to the existing recognized-syntax evaluation logic, which was not touched).
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Six new tests in core/src/language/adl/mod.rs: unrecognized_constraint_syntax_is_diagnosed_not_silently_admitted (ATLAS-E052 present, declaration still recorded with zero checks), unrecognized_constraint_syntax_never_reports_as_passed (constraint_results entry exists, passed:false, ATLAS-E053 present, top-level diagnostics non-empty), empty_constraint_body_is_diagnosed_not_treated_as_vacuously_true, invariants_are_evaluated_just_like_constraints_not_silently_skipped (a deliberately-violated invariant produces a constraint_results entry with passed:false and an ATLAS-E050 diagnostic -- proving it is now actually evaluated, not merely present), a_satisfied_invariant_passes_exactly_like_a_satisfied_constraint (no regression: a correctly-written, satisfied invariant passes cleanly with zero diagnostics), plus the pre-existing constraint_and_materialization_use_observed_graph and parser_accepts_vertical_slice tests re-run unchanged to confirm no regression to already-working recognized-syntax constraints.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Re-ran the fixed compiler against this repository's own real, independently-authored `.atlas/declared/system.adl` (not a synthetic fixture -- the file predates this fix and was not written to exercise it) via `atlas-cli check --root .` and `atlas-cli systemize --root .`: all four of its real constraints (BackendIsRust, CoreIsMaterialized, AdapterIsMaterialized, RuntimeIsMaterialized) still evaluate cleanly with passed:true and zero diagnostics -- proving the fix does not misclassify real, valid, already-recognized constraint syntax. The repository's real ADL currently declares zero `invariant` blocks, so the invariant-evaluation fix's real-world non-regression is established via `docs audit` and `systemize` both still reporting coding_admission.allowed:true and dependency_closure.state:CLOSED (unrelated to invariants, but proving no incidental breakage of the surrounding compile_adl pipeline).

implementation.core_compiler: core/src/language/adl/mod.rs -- parse_constraint_check now returns Result<Vec<ConstraintCheck>, String> (Err carries the unrecognized/empty joined body text) instead of silently returning Vec::new(); its one call site in parse_adl_source's ["constraint", ...] | ["invariant", ...] match arm pushes a new ATLAS-E052 diagnostic on Err, while still recording the ConstraintDecl (with empty checks) for provenance; evaluate_constraints now iterates `declared.constraints.iter().chain(declared.invariants.iter())` instead of `declared.constraints` alone, and pushes a new ATLAS-E053 diagnostic (and forces passed:false) for any declaration whose checks list is empty, before attempting to evaluate its (nonexistent) checks

the same silent-fallback-to-empty-with-implicit-success pattern found here (an unrecognized/unhandled input path defaulting to a trivially-true or trivially-empty result rather than an explicit diagnosed state) is worth keeping in mind as a class of defect when auditing other parser/evaluator pairs in this codebase
overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. Two real correctness defects in the ADL compiler's constraint/invariant handling are fixed: (1) unrecognized constraint/invariant syntax now produces an explicit ATLAS-E052 diagnostic and can never report passed:true (ATLAS-E053 defense-in-depth), directly implementing the canonical rule in ARCHITECTURAL-INTEGRITY.md that unevaluable invariants must read UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE, not PASS; (2) `invariant` declarations are now evaluated by the exact same pass as `constraint` declarations, closing a gap where every invariant in the language was silently excluded from `constraint_results` and therefore invisible to `atlas-cli check`'s readiness gate. Verified against this repository's own real, independently-authored declared system with zero regression to already-working constraints.
